description: A bank, a landlord, an employer, a phone company and a government office will each run their own identity check on the same person in the same month.
energy_note: Verified five times, trusted once each.

aspect: The document you need is with the thing you cannot do
description: Proof of address needs a utility bill; the utility needs an account; the account needs proof of address. The loop is broken by whoever bends first.
energy_note: A circle you have to talk your way out of.

aspect: Certified copies cost money and a trip
description: A notary, a solicitor or a post office charges per document and is open during the hours you are at work.

Two forms of ID, one of which must be dated within three months. His payslip is digital and 'not accepted', the tenancy agreement is in his partner's name, and the branch appointment is eleven days out.
energy_note: Employed, solvent, and unbanked for six weeks.

description: Every proof has a shelf life. The bundle you assembled in March is invalid in August, so the work is done again from scratch.
energy_note: A job you finish and then have to redo.

aspect: How this dataset relates to the other one
description: Everything here is imposed on anyone. The hurdles in assets/text/iran are imposed on top, by nationality and status. The immigration-specific costs are additive to these, not instead of them: an Iranian applicant proves identity to a bank AND to a visa officer, waits in a hospital queue AND in a security screening queue.
energy_note: The same day, plus a second one nobody else has.
notes: Deliberate design: the baseline makes the specific disadvantage measurable.
